text:
If $α$ + $β$ + $γ$ = 2$π$, then the system of equations 

x + (cos $γ$)y + (cos $β$)z = 0

(cos $γ$)x + y + (cos $α$)z = 0

(cos $β$)x  + (cos $α$)y + z = 0

has :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 31st August Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given $α$ + $β$ + $γ$ = 2$π$

$\Delta =\left |\begin{array}{lll} 1 & \cos γ & \cos β \\ \cos γ & 1 & \cos α \\ \cos β & \cos α & 1 \end{array}\right |$

$=1-\cos ^{2}α-\cos γ(\cos γ-\cos α\cos β)+\cos β(\cos α\cos γ-\cos β)$

$=1-\cos ^{2}α-\cos ^{2}β-\cos ^{2}γ+2\cos α\cos β\cos γ$

$=\sin ^{2}α-\cos ^{2}β-\cos γ(\cos γ-2\cos α\cos β)$

$=-\cos (α+β)\cos (α-β)-\cos γ(\cos (2π-(α-β))-2\cos α\cos β)$

$=-\cos (2π-γ)\cos (α-β)-\cos γ(\cos (α+β)-2\cos α\cos β)$

$=-\cos γ\cos (α-β)+\cos γ(\cos α\cos β+\sin α\sin β)$

$=-\cos γ\cos (α-β)+\cos γ\cos (α-β)$

$=0$

So, the system of equation has infinitely many solutions.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 31st August Evening Shift

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 31st August Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$α=\lim _{x\to \frac{π}{4}}\frac{\tan ^{3}x-\tan x}{\cos \left (x+\frac{π}{4}\right )};\frac{0}{0}$ form

Using L Hospital rule

$α=\lim _{x\to \frac{π}{4}}\frac{3\tan ^{2}x\sec ^{2}x-\sec ^{2}x}{-\sin \left (x+\frac{π}{4}\right )}$

$α$ = $-$4

$β=\lim _{x\to 0}(\cos x)^{\cot x}=e^{\lim _{x\to 0}\frac{(\cos x-1)}{\tan x}}$

$β=e^{\lim _{x\to 0}\frac{-(1-\cos x)}{x2}.\frac{x2}{\left (\dfrac{\tan x}{x}\right )x}}$

$β=e^{\lim _{x\to 0}\left (\frac{-1}{2}\right ).\frac{x}{1}}=e^{0}\Rightarrow β=1$

$α$ = $-$4; $β$ = 1

If $ax^{2} + bx$ $-$ 4 = 0 are the roots then

16a $-$ 4b $-$ 4 = 0 & a + b $-$ 4 = 0

$\Rightarrow$ a = 1 & b = 3

text: If $y\frac{dy}{dx}=x\left [\frac{y^{2}}{x^{2}}+\frac{𝜙\left (\frac{y2}{x2}\right )}{𝜙^{'}\left (\frac{y2}{x2}\right )}\right ]$, x > 0, $𝜙$ > 0, and y(1) = $-$1, then $𝜙\left (\frac{y^{2}}{4}\right )$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 31st August Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let, $y=tx$

$\frac{dy}{dx}=t+x\frac{dt}{dx}$

$\therefore$ $tx\left (t+x\frac{dt}{dx}\right )=x\left (t^{2}+\frac{φ(t^{2})}{φ^{'}(t^{2})}\right )$

$t^{2}+xt\frac{dt}{dx}=t^{2}+\frac{φ(t^{2})}{φ^{'}(t^{2})}$

$\int \frac{tφ^{'}(t^{2})}{φ(t^{2})}dt=\int \frac{dx}{x}$

Let $φ(t^{2})=p$

$\therefore$ $φ^{'}(t^{2})2tdt=dp$

$\Rightarrow \int \frac{dy}{2p}=\int \frac{dx}{x}$

$\frac{1}{2}\ln φ(t^{2})=\ln x+\ln c$

$φ(t^{2})=x^{2}k$

$φ\left (\frac{y^{2}}{x^{2}}\right )=kx^{2},φ(1)=k$

$φ\left (\frac{y^{2}}{4}\right )=4φ(1)$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 31st August Evening Shift

text: If z is a complex number such that $\frac{z-i}{z-1}$ is purely imaginary, then the minimum value of | z $-$ (3 + 3i) | is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 31st August Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\frac{z-i}{z-1}$ is purely imaginary number

Let $z=x+iy$

$\therefore$ $\frac{x+i(y-1)}{(x-1)+i(y)}\times \frac{(x-1)-iy}{(x-1)-iy}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{x(x-1)+y(y-1)+i(-y-x+1)}{(x-1)^{2}+y^{2}}$ is purely imaginary number

$\Rightarrow x(x-1)+y(y-1)=0$

$\Rightarrow \left (x-\frac{1}{2}\right )^{2}+\left (y-\frac{1}{2}\right )^{2}=\frac{1}{2}$

 
[IMG]
 

$\therefore$ $|z-(3+3i)|_{\min }=|PC|-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

$=\frac{5}{\sqrt{2}}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}=2\sqrt{2}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 31st August Evening Shift

text: Let A be the set of all points ($α$, $β$) such that the area of triangle formed by the points (5, 6), (3, 2) and ($α$, $β$) is 12 square units. Then the least possible length of a line segment joining the origin to a point in A, is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 31st August Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)
tags: straight lines and pair of straight lines

solution.body:
For the triangle with vertices $(5,6)$, $(3,2)$ and $(α,β)$:

$\dfrac{1}{2}\left |\right |\begin{array}{lll} 5 & 6 & 1 \\ 3 & 2 & 1 \\ α & β & 1 \end{array}\left |\right |=12$

The determinant is $5(2-β)-6(3-α)+(3β-2α)=4α-2β-8$, so $|4α-2β-8|=24$.

Hence $2α-β=16$ or $2α-β=-8$: the set A is the union of the parallel lines $2x-y-16=0$ and $2x-y+8=0$.

The shortest segment from the origin to a point of A is the smaller of the perpendicular distances from the origin to these lines, $\dfrac{16}{\sqrt{5}}$ and $\dfrac{8}{\sqrt{5}}$, which is $\dfrac{8}{\sqrt{5}}$.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 31st August Evening Shift

text:
If [x] is the greatest integer $\leq$ x, then 

$π^{2}\int\limits _{0}^{2}\left (\sin \frac{πx}{2}\right )(x-[x])^{[x]}dx$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 31st August Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$I=π^{2}\int\limits _{0}^{2}\sin \left (\frac{πx}{2}\right )(x-[x])^{[x]}dx$

$=π^{2}\int\limits _{0}^{1}\sin \left (\frac{πx}{2}\right )x^{0}dx+π^{2}\int\limits _{1}^{2}\sin \left (\frac{πx}{2}\right )(x-1)dx$

$=π^{2}\left [\frac{-2}{π}\cos \frac{πx}{2}\right ]_{0}^{1}+π^{2}\left [(x-1)\frac{2}{π}\left (-\cos \frac{πx}{2}\right )\right ]_{1}^{2}+π^{2}\int\limits _{1}^{2}\frac{2}{π}\cos \frac{πx}{2}dx$

$=π^{2}\left (\frac{2}{π}\right )+\frac{2π^{2}}{π}(1-0)+2π.\frac{2}{π}\left (\sin \frac{πx}{2}\right )\left |_{1}^{2} \right.$

$=2π+2π+4(0-1)=4π-4=4(π-1)$

text: The number of 4-digit numbers which are neither multiple of 7 nor multiple of 3 is $____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 31st August Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
A = 4-digit numbers divisible by 3

A = 1002, 1005, ....., 9999.

9999 = 1002 + (n $-$ 1)3

$\Rightarrow$ (n $-$ 1)3 = 8997 $\Rightarrow$ n = 3000

B = 4-digit numbers divisible by 7

B = 1001, 1008, ......., 9996

$\Rightarrow$ 9996 = 1001 + (n $-$ 1)7

$\Rightarrow$ n = 1286

A $\cap$ B = 1008, 1029, ....., 9996

9996 = 1008 + (n $-$ 1)21

$\Rightarrow$ n = 429

So, no divisible by either 3 or 7

= 3000 + 1286 $-$ 429 = 3857

total 4-digits numbers = 9000

required numbers = 9000 $-$ 3857 = 5143

text:
If $\int \frac{\sin x}{\sin ^{3}x+\cos ^{3}x}dx=$ 

$α\log _{e}|1+\tan x|+β\log _{e}|1-\tan x+\tan ^{2}x|+γ\tan ^{-1}\left (\frac{2\tan x-1}{\sqrt{3}}\right )+C$, where C is constant of integration, then the value of $18(α+β+γ^{2})$ is $______________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 31st August Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$=\int \frac{\frac{\sin x}{\cos 3x}}{1+\tan ^{3}x}dx=\int \frac{\tan x.\sec ^{2}x}{(\tan x+1)(1+\tan ^{2}x-\tan x)}dx$

Let $\tan x=t\Rightarrow \sec ^{2}x.dx=dt$

$=\int \frac{t}{(t+1)(t^{2}-t+1)}dt$

$=\int \left (\frac{A}{t+1}+\frac{B(2t-1)}{t^{2}-t+1}+\frac{C}{t^{2}-t+1}\right )dt$

$\Rightarrow A(t^{2}-t+1)+B(2t-1)(t+1)+C(t+1)=t$

$\Rightarrow t^{2}(A+2B)+t(-A+B+C)+A-B+C=t$

$\therefore$ $A+2B=0$ ..... (1)

$-A+B+C=1$ ... (2)

$A-B+C=0$ ... (3)

$\Rightarrow C=\frac{1}{2}\Rightarrow A-B=-\frac{1}{2}$ ... (4)

$A+2B=0$

$A-B=-\frac{1}{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $3B=\frac{1}{2}\Rightarrow B=\frac{1}{6}$

$A=-\frac{1}{3}$

$I=-\frac{1}{3}\int \frac{dt}{1+t}+\frac{1}{6}\int \frac{2t-1}{t^{2}-t+1}dt+\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{dt}{t^{2}-t+1}$

$=-\frac{1}{3}\ln |(1+\tan x)|+\frac{1}{6}\ln |\tan ^{2}x-\tan x+1|+\frac{1}{2}.\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\tan ^{-1}\left (\frac{\left (\tan x-\frac{1}{2}\right )}{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}}\right )$

$=-\frac{1}{3}\ln |(1+\tan x)|+\frac{1}{6}\ln |\tan ^{2}x-\tan x+1|+\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\tan ^{-1}\left (\frac{2\tan x-1}{\sqrt{3}}\right )+C$

$α=-\frac{1}{3},β=\frac{1}{6},γ=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$

$18(α+β+γ^{2})=18\left (-\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{6}+\frac{1}{3}\right )=3$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 31st August Evening Shift

text: The number of elements in the set $\left \{A=\left (\begin{array}{ll} a & b \\ 0 & d \end{array}\right ):a,b,d\in \{-1,0,1\}and(I-A)^{3}=I-A^{3}\right \}$, where I is 2 $\times$ 2 identity matrix, is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 31st August Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$(I-A)^{3}=I^{3}-A^{3}-3A(I-A)=I-A^{3}$

$\Rightarrow 3A(I-A)=0$ or $A^{2}=A$

$\Rightarrow \left [\begin{array}{ll} a^{2} & ab+bd \\ 0 & d^{2} \end{array}\right ]=\left [\begin{array}{ll} a & b \\ 0 & d \end{array}\right ]$

$\Rightarrow a^{2}=a,b(a+d-1)=0,d^{2}=d$

If b $\neq$ 0, a + d = 1 $\Rightarrow$ 4 ways

If b = 0, a = 0, 1 & d = 0, 1 $\Rightarrow$ 4 ways

$\Rightarrow$ Total 8 matrices
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 31st August Evening Shift

text: Let f(x) be a cubic polynomial with f(1) = $-$10, f($-$1) = 6, and has a local minima at x = 1, and f'(x) has a local minima at x = $-$1. Then f(3) is equal to $____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 31st August Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $f(x) = ax^{3} + bx^{2} + cx + d$

$f'(x) = 3ax^{2} + 2bx + c$ $\Rightarrow$ f''(x) = 6ax + 2b

f'(x) has local minima at x = $-$1, so

$\because$ f''($-$1) = 0 $\Rightarrow$ $-$6a + 2b = 0 $\Rightarrow$ b = 3a ..... (i)

f(x) has local minima at x = 1

f'(1) = 0

$\Rightarrow$ 3a + 6a + c = 0

$\Rightarrow$ c = $-$9a ..... (ii)

f(1) = $-$10

$\Rightarrow$ $-$5a + d = $-$10 ..... (iii)

f($-$1) = 6

$\Rightarrow$ 11a + d = 6 ..... (iv)

Solving Eqs. (iii) and (iv)

a = 1, d = $-$5

From Eqs. (i) and (ii),

b = 3, c = $-$9

$\therefore$ $f(x) = x^{3} + 3x^{2}$ $-$ 9x $-$ 5

So, f(3) = 27 + 27 $-$ 27 $-$ 5 = 22
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 31st August Evening Shift
